questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Three lakhs of people (1)/ attended the workshop (2)/ held at Ramleela ground. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the preposition ‘of’ is incorrect here and needs to be omitted. The word ‘lakhs’ in plural form is incorrect too as it is used to denote the number of ‘people’. It should read as:’Three lakh people..’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Ayesha is among the few people (1)/ in the office which did not (2)/ blindly follow the path of other. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as ‘which’ is used to refer to inanimate objects and here the subject is a person so the correct word here would be ‘who’. It should read as:’.in the office who did not..’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I would (1)/ rather to (2)/ die than beg. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'rather' and 'than' are** correlative conjunctions** i.e., they are always used in **pair**.
 
• The preposition 'to' never agrees with the conjunction 'rather'.
 
 
• For example: I would **rather** watch a movie than sleep.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, the use of the preposition ‘to’ after ‘rather' is incorrect.
 
• Removing 'to' after 'rather' would make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is:* I would **rather die** than beg.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Some of the important **Correlative Conjunctions** are:

 
 
• Either….or
 
• Neither….nor
 
• Hardly….when
 
• Scarcely….when
 
• Both…and
 
• If…then
 
• Not only….but also
 
• **Rather….than**
 
• Whether…or
 
• No sooner…than
 
• Else…but
 
• Lest…should
 
• Other…than
 
• So…that

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Ankit cannot (1)/ succeed because (2)/ he labours hard. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the conjunction ‘because’ is incorrect here and should be replaced with ‘unless.’

‘Because’ is used to state the reason why a person cannot do something. The conjunction ‘unless’ means ‘except if (used to introduce the case in which a statement being made is not true or valid).’

questions.solution: The sentence has no error. It has been structured correctly. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Hundreds of _________ have been used in the study of the past and of man's progress.
questions.solution:
The word here should be that which is used to study something. Thus ‘stories’ and ‘tales’ which means ‘stories’ are incorrect here. ‘Methods’ which means ‘processes’ is the correct fit here. ‘Motions’ means ‘movements’ and makes no sense here.

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

One of the pens ______ no ink.
questions.solution: The verb with ‘one of the’ is always singular as it refers to one single subject. Thus ‘has’ is the correct answer. ‘Has’ is used to refer to the possession of an object by something. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

This is the same dog ______ was running on the road.
questions.solution:
‘Who’ and ‘whom’ are used in cases of human beings and not animals.The correct word here is ‘that’ and not ‘which’.

 A defining clause (also called an essential clause or a restrictive clause) gives information essential to the meaning of the sentence. *That* is used in defining clauses. Here’s an example:

My bike that has a broken seat is in the garage.

*Which* introduces non-defining clauses. Unlike defining clauses, non-defining clauses (also called nonessential or nonrestrictive clauses) don’t limit the meaning of the sentence. You might lose interesting details if you remove them, but the meaning of the sentence wouldn’t change. Sometimes, these phrases are set off by commas.

My bike, which has a broken seat, is in the garage.

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Loiter
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2: **Punctual**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• Loiter means to wander**, **walk, or move in a leisurely or aimless way.
 
• **Punctual **means happening or doing something at the agreed or proper time.
 
• The synonyms of the given word 'loiter' are "**crawl, creep, dally, dawdle, delay, diddle, dillydally".**
 
• The antonyms of the given word 'loiter' are "**fly, hasten, hotfoot, hurry, race, rip, rocket, run, rush, scoot, scud, scurry, speed".**
 
• The antonym of the given word **'loiter**' is 'Punctual' since both have the opposite meaning.
 
• Let us look at the meanings of the options- 
 
 
 

 WORDS
 MEANING
 
 

 wander
 walk, or move in a leisurely or aimless way. 
 
 

 **Sober**
 serious and calm.
 
 

 Free

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The red and (the white rose) looks beautiful.
questions.solution: The verb in the sentence has a singular verb ‘looks’ thus the subject here should be singular as well. Thus the article ‘the’ cannot be used here. ‘The red and the white rose’ would mean two roses;one red and one white. Thus it should read as:’The red and white rose.’

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question: Life priorities and ______ are never going
questions.solution: The word here should be such that is a common part of life and cannot be eliminated at any cost. Thus ‘necessities’ which means ‘needs’ is the correct word here. The other words do not fit here.The word ‘passions’ means ‘strong and barely controllable emotion.’

questions.question: make some time for ______ the well being of the environment
questions.solution: One should ‘ensure’ or ‘make sure’ the well being of one’s environment thus option 1 is the correct answer. One cannot result it or develop it. Well-being of the environment cannot be ‘enlarged’ as well. It means ‘to increase the size.’

questions.question: save our environment, ______ life changing movement
questions.solution: The word ‘no’ is the correct word as the next sentence has the word ‘if’. It has a condition which conveys the meaning that no big step is required to save the environment. Thus ‘huge’ which means ‘big’ and ‘sufficient’ which means ‘adequate’ would not fit here.

questions.question: that is will power honest ______ and some small initiatives
questions.solution: The word in the blank must be a noun that goes with the adjective ‘honest.’ Thus ‘inclination’ which means ‘propensity’ which is similar to will power fits here correctly. The other words do not convey any meaning here. ‘Assurance’ means ‘a positive declaration intended to give confidence’ and ‘factor’ means ‘a circumstance, fact, or influence that contributes to a result.’

questions.question: It's a very ______ element of our environment.
questions.solution: The passage tells us to save water and not waste it thus it is clear that water is very important. The word ‘precious’ therefore fits here correctly. The word ‘contradictory’ means ‘mutually opposed or inconsistent’ and ‘bulky’ means ‘heavy.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: If I am a cultural, well-behaved Indian, what won't I do?

options.text: Touch the feets of the elders.
Wake up early in the morning, especially on the festive occasions.
Shake my head as a habit while talking.

questions.solution: All the options except 3 are mentioned in the passage. Thus option 3 has the activity which does not fit in.

questions.question: Why is India called a unity in diversity?

options.text: Different groups of people co-operate with each other.
People of different sects, caste and religion live together.

questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage that India has people of different sects,castes and religions live together. It is a strength of India but the reason of calling it so is not this. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true according to the passage?

options.text: Culture entails what drawing people draw.

questions.solution: All of the options are mentioned in the passage except option 4. It is mentioned ‘It entails how they dress, how they speak, the type of food they eat, the manner in which they worship, and their art among many other things.’Thus option 4 is not true according to the passage.

questions.question: **Based on the above passage, which of the following is NOT true about Indian culture?**

options.text: Indian culture dates back to 3300 BC – 1300 BC.
Envy religion follows their own tradition and customs.
Every religion is treated equally in India.
In India there is unity in diversity.

questions.solution: All the options are mentioned in the passage except option 2. It is not written that every religion has its own traditions and customs. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What is the reason behind the immense variety in Indian culture?
questions.solution: The immense variety in Indian culture is due to the huge population present here. Every region is different from one another. This contributes to the immense variety in culture. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.
